events.title: VALERIUS'S RECORD IS ASSEMBLED INTO A SINGLE PETITION FOR FORMAL RECOGNITION
events.body: Gaius Maximus Valerius has assembled the scattered records of his recent career into a single petition for formal recognition of his expanded standing and estate administration. Military reports, supply records, boundary surveys, collection schedules, and production registers are arranged chronologically so that each claim can be checked against an underlying record. Rather than relying on gifts or a public distribution of money, the petition places the weight of its case on Valerius's documented conduct as a commander, administrator, and landholder. Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer and Marcus Claudius Marcellus receive copies of the compiled material and agree to place it before additional political contacts. The size of the dossier itself becomes part of the story, because it gives Valerius's supporters something concrete to present rather than merely a favorable personal account. The submission therefore enters the Roman political world as a record requiring examination, not as a claim that recognition has already been granted.

events.title: FORMER OFFICERS AND ESTATE ADMINISTRATORS PROVIDE WRITTEN TESTIMONY ON VALERIUS'S SERVICE
events.body: Written testimony begins arriving from men who served alongside Valerius or worked under his administrative arrangements. Former officers describe the practical handling of detachments, supplies, patrol responsibilities, and the discipline expected during difficult operations, while estate administrators describe the newer collection and production systems. Several statements are deliberately narrow, identifying particular duties and periods rather than praising Valerius in general terms. That limitation gives the testimony a more documentary character and allows the petition's supporters to attach individual statements to specific entries in the larger record. The testimony does not settle the question of formal recognition, but it gives outside readers additional material with which to test the petition. By the end of the week, the dossier contains a growing collection of independent accounts rather than a single self-authored narrative.

events.title: MERCHANTS AND LANDHOLDERS BEGIN CITING VALERIUS'S RECORD WITHOUT BEING ASKED
events.body: Several merchants and neighboring landholders begin referring to Valerius's record in conversations concerning the newly organized estates and their commercial connections. Their comments are not presented as a coordinated political campaign, and no organized distribution of gifts accompanies them. Instead, the references focus on predictable collections, functioning roads, reliable estate administration, and the fact that the new holdings have been put back to work rather than left idle. A merchant connected with the lake-port trade reportedly points to the regularity of Valerius's arrangements as a reason that contracts can be discussed with greater confidence. Nearby landholders likewise describe the security arrangements as less disruptive than the conditions that preceded them. The unsolicited attention broadens the circle of people who know of Valerius's record, even though it produces no formal decision on his petition.

events.title: CELER REQUESTS A PRECISE ACCOUNT OF VALERIUS'S MILITARY SERVICE
events.body: Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer sends word that the political review now requires a more exact account of Valerius's military service. The request asks for dates, command responsibilities, supply arrangements, and the disposition of the men under his authority, rather than another general statement of achievement. Valerius's administrators begin matching the request against older reports and the surviving campaign registers. The work forces several late-night reviews of records that had previously been maintained for practical use rather than political presentation. Celer's request is treated as a sign that the dossier is being examined seriously, but it also makes clear that favorable connections will not remove the need for documentation. The petition consequently moves into a more exacting stage in which individual claims must withstand detailed questions.

events.title: MARCELLUS CARRIES VALERIUS'S ADMINISTRATIVE RECORD INTO A WIDER POLITICAL CIRCLE
events.body: Marcus Claudius Marcellus carries the administrative portion of Valerius's record into a wider circle of Roman political contacts. The material emphasizes the fixed collection calendar, the separation of estate operating funds from other obligations, the witnessed land surveys, and the restoration of productive acreage. Marcellus presents the records as evidence of a sustained pattern rather than as isolated successes from a single campaign. Several recipients ask to see the supporting registers before offering any opinion, and copies of the most relevant entries are therefore prepared for further circulation. The process remains deliberately documentary, with no announcement of a granted honor or office. By Christmas, Valerius's name is reaching more political readers through written records than through direct personal solicitation.

events.title: THE YEAR-END ESTATE REVIEW FINDS THE NEW RECORDS CONSISTENT WITH THE OLDER REGISTERS
events.body: At year's end, Valerius orders another review of the estate registers so that the political dossier will not rest on newly prepared figures alone. Administrators compare the latest production and collection records with older registers covering the principal estate, the lake-port holding, the former bandit lands, and the recently surveyed expansion. The review identifies no material discrepancy requiring a correction to the current working accounts. The finding does not transform the records into proof of perfection, but it allows the newer material to be presented alongside the older documentation without an obvious contradiction. The same review also confirms that the expanded acreage remains under active administration rather than merely appearing on a boundary map. Valerius therefore closes the year with a record that has survived another internal examination while the formal political review remains unfinished.

events.title: VALERIUS'S PETITION ENTERS THE NEW YEAR WITH SUPPORT BUILT AROUND HIS RECORDED SERVICE
events.body: The final days of December leave Valerius's petition still under review, but its supporting circle is now larger than it was at the beginning of the month. Celer and Marcellus continue examining the material while additional correspondents have begun asking for particular records rather than simply expressing general approval. The distinction matters to Valerius's political effort: his case is advancing through accumulated evidence of military service, administration, property management, and economic order rather than through a traditional campaign of plebeian patronage. No formal recognition is announced before the year's end, and the petition remains subject to whatever further scrutiny its recipients choose to apply. Valerius's administrators nevertheless finish the year with the records organized for rapid response to additional questions. The new year therefore opens with his political standing under active consideration, supported by a growing documentary record but without a final official determination.
